A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Data-Juicer Sandbox work. All 31 pages of v2 and 33 pages of v3, including appendices, support comparison through text extraction and visual inspection.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E report original MGM, EasyAnimate, CLIP and T2V-Turbo experiments, including operator comparisons, scaling results and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds captioning, iterative refinement, mapper and prompt-adjustment results.

M1.justification: Appendix E.12 introduces an inference hook and a workflow for evaluating generated prompt candidates across checkpoints. The core Probe-Analyze-Refine procedure, pooling strategies and T2V training losses remain unchanged; mapper operators were already supported in v2.

E1.justification: v3 adds an explicit image-captioning fine-tuning and caption-generation use case alongside the retained image-understanding, video-generation and CLIP tasks. Captioning data sources are not clearly identified, so additional dataset or domain coverage cannot be established.

E2.justification: The retained experiments use the same baselines and VBench comparator membership, including LaVie-2 and Vchitect 2.0 despite updated citations. InternVL is an experimental model; the new mapper and prompt comparisons test workflow variants rather than additional competing algorithms.

E3.justification: v3 adds an InternVL evaluation across 1B, 2B, 4B and 26B parameters, with captioning data pools spanning 24k–189k samples and one training epoch (Table 5). Appendices E.10–E.12 introduce checkpoint-continuation experiments, mapper substitutions and ten alternative prompts. The previously documented MGM, EasyAnimate and CLIP settings are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses test operator-ranking stability after further training, image regeneration versus recaptioning, and prompt sensitivity across checkpoints (E.10–E.12). v3 also adds tagged word clouds, CLIP operator correlations and a qualitative mapper example. The original entropy, correlation and T2V ablation analyses remain.

E5.justification: Appendices D.2, D.4 and D.5 retain the same repetition, seed and standard-deviation reporting. Mapper results reuse mean-plus-deviation reporting; no new statistical estimation or significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: v3 adds captioning rankings and scaling curves, second-iteration rankings, and prompt-dependent results. Table 15 newly reports mapper changes of +13.45 ± 11.33% for image regeneration and -1.07 ± 0.65% for recaptioning. Existing MGM, CLIP and VBench results are retained; these additions are not same-setting improvements over v2.

T1.justification: The pooling definitions, cost discussion and Hoeffding-bound argument in Section 3.2 and Appendix C are unchanged. The evaluation, entropy and T2V loss equations are also retained without substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract newly emphasizes experimentally demonstrated extensibility, and the introduction adds a claim of scaling behavior from 1B to 26B parameters. The central sandbox, workflow, transferability and VBench-leading contribution claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations concerning caption quality, regeneration as denoising, and checkpoint-dependent operator and prompt choices. The conclusion removes v2's explicit resource-limited qualification about testing larger CLIP models. Most existing interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New material documents checkpoint continuation, diffusion/BLIP mapper backends, Qwen2.5-max prompt generation, inference-hook modifications and the exact tested prompts. Existing implementation sections remain largely unchanged, while captioning dataset sources and evaluation details remain unclear.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations for InternVL and Trinity-RFT and expands the contrast with DataComp to post-training and iterative co-development in E.10. Most other reference edits, including RedPajama, Vchitect and LaVie, update existing works rather than introduce new research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 makes targeted edits to the abstract, introduction, use-case overview, scaling discussion and conclusion. It adds a Section 4.6 roadmap and replaces the appendix's prose guide with a table of contents; most retained prose and section ordering remain stable.

P2.justification: The appendix changes substantially from single-column to two-column layout, shrinking and relocating several heatmaps. Figures 2 and 3 gain captioning panels, while new word clouds, correlation displays, a mapper example and Tables 8 and 14–16 expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The mapper, iterative and prompt experiments provide useful evidence beyond v2's filter-focused validation. However, captioning data and evaluation details remain unclear, and Figure 9 contains Figure 7's 22-by-22 T2V correlation values under different operator labels. E.10 also claims eight overlapping top-ten operators whereas Table 14 shows seven. These additions and reporting problems prevent a reliable judgment of net overall quality.
